plan: My private value is $9. In a second-price sealed auction with three bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. Since the values are independently drawn and this is a single round, I'll bid exactly my private value of $9.

My private value is $20. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. Since the bid is sealed and I want to maximize expected profit, bidding $20 means:
- If my bid wins, I'll pay less than my value
- If my bid loses, I pay nothing
- Bidding above $20 risks paying more than my value
- Bidding below $20 risks losing when I could have won profitably

My private value is $20. In a first-price sealed bid auction with three bidders, I want to bid strategically. Since values are randomly drawn, I'll aim to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. A bid around $18-19 gives me a good chance of winning while preserving some potential profit margin. I'll choose $18.50 to balance winning probability and potential earnings.
